name: satsuma-lang
//packageManager: Present because Turborepo refuses to resolve the workspace without being
told which package manager owns it. It is not a version gate: corepack is
not enabled anywhere in this repo or its CI, so npm itself ignores the
field, and Turborepo reads only the name from it. The version records the
npm this repo is developed against. The modern `devEngines.packageManager`
alternative was tried first and rejected — Turborepo rejects any range
spanning more than one npm major, which a range wide enough to cover both
a contributor's npm and the one bundled with CI's Node image must.
//scripts: build:all and test:all are thin aliases over `turbo run`. They exist so the
pre-commit hook, CI and a developer all reach the same task graph, and so the
--filter exclusion on test:all is stated once rather than remembered.
build:all runs `compile` as well as `build` because otherwise the workspace it
leaves behind is not fully built. Only @satsuma/lsp defines `compile` (it is a
no-op elsewhere), and that package's test suite loads per-module files from
dist/ that only tsc produces — its `build` is an esbuild bundle. Omitting
compile here left `npm --prefix tooling/satsuma-lsp test` failing on a
freshly-installed workspace, and failed CI's test-stats job, which spawns
exactly that command. Note this makes dist/server.js the tsc module rather
than the bundle, since compile is ordered after build. That is what the
pre-Turborepo `pretest` hook also left behind, and it is why
scripts/build-artifacts.sh packs the LSP after calling that package's own
`build` directly rather than going through here (see mbt-oy6n).
The remaining exclusion is about *where* a suite can run, not what it covers:
tree-sitter-satsuma's `test` shells out to `tree-sitter test --wasm`, which
needs a writable compiler cache and is invoked with its own environment and
graceful-skip handling by scripts/run-repo-checks.sh.
@satsuma/viz-harness is deliberately NOT excluded: its `test` is Playwright,
which now runs headless Chromium inside the agent sandbox (AGENTS.md) and in
its own CI job, so test:all covers it like every other package.
test:scripts replaces the old test:release, which named
scripts/release-metadata.test.mjs alone while two sibling suites sat beside it
unrun — scripts/generate-test-stats.test.mjs, and the workspace-build-graph
suite R4 added. A glob means the next root-level test file is run by virtue of
existing rather than by someone remembering to name it here.
clean:all removes two Turborepo paths. `tooling/*/.turbo` holds the per-task
logs, which are always worktree-local. `.turbo` is the content-hash cache, and
that entry only bites in the primary worktree: from a linked one under
.worktrees/, turbo shares the primary worktree's cache ('using shared worktree
cache') and this removes nothing. That is not a gap to work around — the cache
is keyed on input hashes, so a restored output is byte-identical to a rebuilt
one and a stale entry cannot produce a wrong answer. To prove a genuinely cold
build, use `turbo run build --force` rather than trying to delete the cache.

scripts.clean:all: rm -rf node_modules tooling/*/node_modules tooling/*/dist tooling/satsuma-cli/src/generated tooling/tree-sitter-satsuma/build tooling/tree-sitter-satsuma/tree-sitter-satsuma.wasm .turbo tooling/*/.turbo
scripts.reinstall: npm run clean:all && npm run install:all
scripts.lint: npm run lint:js && npm run lint:md && npm run lint:yaml && npm run lint:python
scripts.lint:python: ruff check scripts/ tooling/tree-sitter-satsuma/scripts/ skills/ smoke-tests/ evals/phase-0.5-probe/runner/ && ruff format --check scripts/ tooling/tree-sitter-satsuma/scripts/ skills/ smoke-tests/ evals/phase-0.5-probe/runner/
scripts.format: prettier --write "**/*.{ts,mts,cts,js,mjs,cjs}" && ruff format scripts/ tooling/tree-sitter-satsuma/scripts/ skills/ smoke-tests/ evals/phase-0.5-probe/runner/

//devDependencies: commander is not used by anything at the root. It is declared here purely to
control hoisting: katex (a transitive dependency of markdownlint-cli2) pins
commander@^8.3.0, and npm hoisted that to the root node_modules while failing
to nest the ^15.0.0 satsuma-cli requires — `npm ls` reported the tree invalid
and the CLI silently loaded v8. A root declaration makes npm hoist v15 and
nest v8 under katex instead. Remove it once katex no longer pins commander@8.
See feature 42 R2; `npm ls commander` must report no 'invalid' entry.
